methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study of 138 advanced gastric cancer patients stratified by splenic volume change (ΔSV >14% vs ≤14%). A priori sample size calculation conducted. Statistical methods appropriate: Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards regression with multivariate analysis, restricted cubic spline analysis, internal validation with bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions) and 5-fold cross-validation (50 repetitions). C-index assessment with optimism correction demonstrates robust model performance (apparent 0.775, optimism-corrected 0.756, cross-validation 0.752). Sensitivity analyses performed for heterogeneous follow-up intervals with consistent results.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b) investigating prognostic value of CT-based imaging biomarker for risk stratification in immunotherapy-treated gastric cancer. Direct clinical relevance: identifies patients at higher risk of progression and mortality to inform treatment intensity and surveillance. Median OS difference of 12 months between groups (30.9 vs 18.9 months) represents clinically meaningful outcome difference. Nomogram provides practical tool for individualized patient counseling and treatment planning.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods comprehensively reported including CT acquisition parameters (tube voltage, collimation, slice thickness), splenic volume measurement protocol with formula specification, and follow-up procedures. Patient inclusion/exclusion criteria clearly detailed. Statistical methods explicitly described with rationale for cutoff determination (survminer package in R). However, no specific reporting standard referenced (neither STROBE nor cancer-specific guidelines mentioned). No data availability statement provided; code/analysis scripts not shared. Sensitivity analysis methodology transparent.

novelty_literature.justification: First study examining ΔSV as prognostic biomarker in gastric cancer with immunotherapy; prior work documented splenic volume changes in other malignancies (renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic cancer, colorectal cancer). Main finding that splenic enlargement predicts poorer outcomes is consistent with existing literature on splenic volume and immune dysfunction. Integration of ΔSV into nomogram is incremental rather than breakthrough; mechanistic understanding remains correlative without immune profiling.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear motivation for studying understudied imaging biomarker. Methods logically presented with detailed CT protocols and measurement procedures. Results systematically organized with separate sections for inter-observer agreement, baseline characteristics, survival analysis, and model validation. Discussion effectively contextualizes findings within broader literature, acknowledges limitations (retrospective design, single-center, heterogeneous etiology), and proposes future directions including prospective multicenter validation and immune profiling.

key_strengths: Comprehensive prognostic model development with internal validation showing robust discrimination and calibration (C-index 0.756 after optimism correction)
Clinically meaningful outcome differences (OS 30.9 vs 18.9 months) supporting prognostic utility of ΔSV
Novel application to gastric cancer immunotherapy context; clear demonstration that splenic volume elevation is independent prognostic factor after multivariate adjustment
Thorough sensitivity analyses addressing heterogeneous follow-up intervals and temporal standardization; nomogram provides practical risk stratification tool
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with selection bias; exclusion criteria targeting patients with complete imaging may enrich favorable phenotypes
Mechanistic understanding limited by lack of immune profiling; observed associations correlative rather than establishing causation regarding MDSC accumulation or immune exhaustion
Confounding by concurrent chemotherapy not fully addressed; splenic volume changes may reflect chemotherapy effects rather than immunotherapy-specific mechanisms
External validation needed before clinical implementation; geographic limitation (China-based cohorts) limits generalizability to Western populations
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid Tier 3 prognostic study with robust internal validation methodology and clinical relevance for risk stratification. Single-center design and lack of external validation prevent higher tier acceptance. Appropriate for specialist journal focused on gastric cancer or immunotherapy outcomes.
